data.title: Still Life with Flowers

thumbnail.alt_text: A work made of oil on canvas.

data.credit_line: Gift of Mary and Leigh Block
data.publication_history:
Claude Roger-Marx, "Odilon Redon ou les droits de l'imagination," Feuillets d'art 5 (1919): ill. op. sit. 36.

Katherine Grant Sterne, "Odilon Redon Viewed Again," Parnassus 3, no. 3 (Mar. 1931): 8, as Flowers and Butterflies.

"Important REdons in the United States," Parnassus 3, no. 4 (Apr. 1931): 17, as Flowers and Butterflies.

Klaus Berger, Odilon Redon: Fantady and Color (New York; Toronto; London: McGraw-Hill, 1965), 2023, as Anemones with Butterflies.

Jean Cassou, Odilon Redon (Paris: Fratelli Fabbri, 1972), 62–63, fig. 2, as Vaso con Flori e farfalle.

Douglas Druick, et. al., Odilon Redon: Prince of Dreams, 1840–1916 (New York: Harry Abrams, 1996), 320–22, 325, fig. 5.

Alec Wildenstein, Catalogue Raisonné de l'Oeuvre Peint vol. 3 (Paris: 1996), 144, no. 1572.
data.exhibition_history:
Galerie Barbazanges, Esposition Retrospective d'oeurves d'Odlon REdon, May–June 1920, cat. 80 as Anemones.

Paris, Hotel de la Curiosité et des Beaux-Arts, 1re Exposition de Collectionneurs, Mar. 10–Apr. 10, 1924, cat. 236, as Bouquet.

Paris, Musée des Arts Décoratifs, Odilon Redon: Expisition Retrospective de son Oeurve, Mar. 1926, 70, as Fleurs et Papillons.

New York, De Hauke and Co., Paintings, Pastels, Drawings, Water Colors, Lithographs by Odilon Redon, Nov. 1928, cat. 18, as Fleurs et Papillons.

New York, Museum of Modern Art, Tenth Loan Exhibition: Lautres, Redon, Feb. 1–Mar. 2, 1931, cat. 88, as Flowers and Butterflies.

New York, Museum of Modern Art, Fruit and Flower Paintins, Mar. 15–25, 1933, no cat.

Washington, D.C., Museum of Modern Art Gallery of Washington, Flowers and Gruits, Mar. 29–May 1, 1938, cat. 42, as Flowers and Butterflies.

Art Institute of Chicago, Chicago's Dream, A World's Treasure, 1893–1993, Nov. 1, 1993–Jan. 9, 1994, no cat.

Kunsthalle Bremen, Paula Modersohn-Becker und die Kunst in Paris um 1900–Von Cézanne bis Picasso, Oct. 13, 2007–Feb. 24, 2008, cat. 160.
data.provenance_text: Armand Parent, Paris, by 1920 until at least 1926 [Paris 1920 and Paris 1926]. Mrs. Cornelius N. Bliss, Jr. (died 1966; born Zaidee C. Cobb), New York, by 1928 until at least 1938 [New York 1928 and Washington, D.C. 1938]. Probably given to her son, Anthony Addison Bliss (1913–1991), New York [this and the following according to Wildenstein 1966]. Possibly Macbeth Gallery, New York, around 1935. Possibly Jacques Seligmann, New York. Wildenstein. Mr. and Mrs. Leigh Block, Santa Barbara and Chicago, by 1982 [according to a 1982 inventory of their Santa Barbara residence; copy in curatorial file]; given to the Art Institute of Chicago, 1988.
